Compare fitted underdispersed-count models

Source: R/family.R
compare_models.Rd

Compares fitted models from this package — cpb, cpb_fe, hurdle_cpb, zi_cpb, gec, gec_fe, hurdle_gec, zi_gec, count_reg, hurdle_count, and zi_count, in any combination of fixed effects and robust/clustered standard errors — on information criteria and, where a predicted distribution is available, on proper scores. Unlike zi_test() this is not a hypothesis test: the models need not be nested, so it is the appropriate tool for the non-nested hurdle-versus-mixture choice. Passing an object that is not a fitted model from this package is an error, and models fit on different data raise a warning.

Usage

compare_models(...)

Arguments

...

Two or more fitted models of the classes above, optionally named. With frequency weights, BIC uses the weight total (nobs()).

Value

A data frame with df, logLik, AIC, BIC, and (where the predicted distribution is available) logscore and rps, one row per model, ordered by AIC, and the flags truncated (a zero-truncated likelihood, conditional on Y >= 1) and separated (a zero-inflation or participation equation the data do not bound, whose log-likelihood is a supremum along a divergent ridge; see zi_cpb(), Separation). The function warns when the models mix truncated and untruncated likelihoods, whose log-likelihoods are of different events, or when a model is separated.

Degrees of freedom

Each model's df is its own (logLik()'s). The hurdle and zero-inflated fits do not count the parameters of a unit with no positive count: with unit fixed effects in the participation or zero equation (part_fe, zero_fe) or in the count equation (fe; dummies written into a formula are covariates to the fit and are counted), such a unit's dummy and its count effect sit at their limits, where every one of its rows has probability one, so it adds nothing to the likelihood. As fixest leaves such units out of a fixed-effects fit, these parameters are left out of df, so that a hurdle and a zero-inflated model fit to the same panel are charged alike. The fits record the units (part_zero_units in the hurdles; zero_units and zero_fe_zero_units in zi_cpb(); fe_zero_units and zero_fe_zero_units in zi_count(); zero_fe_zero_units in zi_gec()), and their print methods give the number. In new data (predict(), score(), cv_score()) the hurdles give such a unit's rows the participation probability at that limit, zero, as the zero-inflated fits give them a count effect at its limit. A unit whose every count is positive has its hurdle participation dummy at the other limit, plus infinity; that dummy is counted, as the zero-inflated fits count their zero-equation dummy for the unit, and in new data the hurdles give the unit's rows the participation probability one (the fits record these units in part_one_units). The zero-inflated fits give a zero_fe unit's rows the structural-zero probability at its limit in the same way: one for a unit with no positive count, zero for a unit whose every count is positive (zero_fe_one_units). CPB fits on the floor support (support = "floor") count these parameters, and in new data evaluate these units at the coefficients the fit stopped at.

The rule is the two-part fits'. The single-equation fixed-effects fits (cpb_fe(), gec_fe(), count_reg(fe = )) count every unit's effect, a unit with no positive count included; set beside a two-part fit to the same panel, such a fit is charged two AIC points per unit with no positive count that the two-part fit is not, and compare_models() says so in a message.

See also

zi_test(), compare_dispersion()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 400; x <- rnorm(n); z <- rnorm(n)
y <- rhurdle_cpb(n, exp(1.2 + 0.5 * x), 0.5, plogis(-0.2 + 0.8 * z))
d <- data.frame(y = y, x = x, z = z)
compare_models(hurdle = hurdle_cpb(y ~ x, data = d, participation = ~ z),
               zi = zi_cpb(y ~ x, data = d, zero = ~ z))
#>        df    logLik      AIC      BIC logscore       rps truncated separated
#> hurdle  5 -552.8141 1115.628 1135.586 1.382035 0.9930062     FALSE     FALSE
#> zi      5 -555.1695 1120.339 1140.296 1.387924 0.9981824     FALSE     FALSE
# }
